question: Which prophet who saw God's throne am I?
reference: Isaiah 6; 7; 36-39 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Isaiah')

clues: I prophesied in Judah during the reigns of four kings, ending with Hezekiah.
In a vision I saw the throne of God and cried that I was a man of unclean lips.
I told King Ahaz that a young woman would give birth to a son called Immanuel.
I foretold a suffering servant who would be pierced for others' transgressions.

question: Which weeping prophet am I?
reference: Jeremiah 1; 36-38 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Jeremiah', p. 31)

clues: God told me he knew me and set me apart before I was formed in the womb.
I was often called weeping over the coming ruin of my nation.
The king cut up and burned my scroll, so my scribe Baruch wrote it again.
I was lowered into a muddy cistern and later rescued by an Ethiopian court official.

question: Which prophet by the river Chebar am I?
reference: Ezekiel 1; 37 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Ezekiel')

clues: I prophesied among the Jewish exiles by the river Chebar in Babylonia.
My opening vision was of four living creatures and wheels full of eyes.
God had me act out the siege of Jerusalem using a brick and a griddle.
In a valley of dry bones, I watched them come together and live again.

question: Which king anointed by Samuel am I?
reference: 1 Samuel 9-15; 28 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Saul No. 1', p. 871)

clues: I went looking for my father's lost donkeys and found a kingdom instead.
I stood a head taller than anyone in Israel.
I lost God's favor after offering a sacrifice I was not authorized to make.
The night before my last battle, I consulted a spirit medium at En-dor.

question: Which Babylonian king am I?
reference: Daniel 2-4 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Nebuchadnezzar', p. 481)

clues: I ruled the empire that destroyed Jerusalem and its temple.
Daniel told me the meaning of my dream about a statue of many metals.
I threw three Hebrews into a superheated furnace and saw a fourth figure with them.
For seven periods I lived like a wild animal until my sanity returned.

question: Which apostle to the nations am I?
reference: Acts 9; 16; 22 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Paul', p. 585)

clues: I was a Pharisee, born in Tarsus, and a Roman citizen by birth.
I guarded the coats of the men who stoned Stephen.
A blinding light on the Damascus road changed the course of my life.
I made three long missionary journeys and wrote letters to many congregations.

question: Which one of the seven am I?
reference: Acts 6-7 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Stephen')

clues: I was one of seven men chosen to help with the daily food distribution.
My opponents could not withstand the wisdom with which I spoke.
On trial, I gave a long review of Israel's history to the Sanhedrin.
As I was stoned, I saw heaven open and asked God not to charge them with the sin.

question: Which prophetess and judge am I?
reference: Judges 4-5 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Deborah')

clues: I was a prophetess who judged Israel, holding court under a palm tree.
I summoned Barak to lead ten thousand men against Sisera's army.
I told Barak the honor of the victory would go to a woman, not to him.
After the battle, I sang a victory song with Barak.

question: Which praying mother am I?
reference: 1 Samuel 1-2 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Hannah')

clues: I was childless, and my husband's other wife taunted me over it.
At the sanctuary in Shiloh I prayed so intensely the priest Eli thought I was drunk.
I vowed that if God gave me a son, I would give him back for lifelong service.
My son grew up to anoint Israel's first two kings.

question: Which Assyrian capital am I?
reference: Jonah 3; Nahum 1-3 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Nineveh')

clues: I was the great capital of the Assyrian Empire, on the Tigris River.
A reluctant prophet was sent to warn me of destruction in forty days.
My king and people fasted in sackcloth, and the calamity was held back.
Generations later the prophet Nahum foretold my fall, and I was destroyed.

question: Which ancient Syrian capital am I?
reference: Acts 9 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Damascus')

clues: I am one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities, capital of ancient Syria.
Saul of Tarsus was traveling toward me with letters to arrest Christians.
A disciple named Ananias was sent to restore the sight of that traveler.
Saul later escaped my walls by being lowered in a basket through a window.

question: Which grandson of Abraham am I?
reference: Genesis 25-35 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Jacob')

clues: I was the younger twin, born gripping my brother's heel.
I traded a bowl of stew for my brother's birthright.
I wrestled a messenger of God until daybreak and would not let go without a blessing.
My name was changed to Israel, and my twelve sons became the tribes.

question: Which righteous sufferer am I?
reference: Job 1-2; 42 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Job', p. 81)

clues: I lived in the land of Uz and was the greatest man of the East.
In a single day I lost my livestock, my servants, and all ten of my children.
Painful boils covered me from head to foot, and I scraped myself with a piece of pottery.
Three friends came to comfort me but ended up accusing me instead.

question: Which prophet of the northern kingdom am I?
reference: Hosea 1-3 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Hosea')

clues: I prophesied to the ten-tribe kingdom in its final decades.
God told me to marry a woman who would be unfaithful to me.
My children were given names meaning judgment and rejection as living signs.
My message was that God's love would still call an unfaithful nation back.

question: Which apostle from Cana am I?
reference: John 1:45-51 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Nathanael')

clues: A friend told me he had found the one Moses and the prophets wrote about.
I asked whether anything good could come out of Nazareth.
Jesus said he had seen me under a fig tree before we ever met.
I am generally thought to be the same apostle called Bartholomew.

question: Which shepherd king am I?
reference: 1 Samuel 16-17; 2 Samuel 11-12 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'David')

clues: I was the youngest son, out watching the sheep when the prophet came to anoint me.
I played the harp to soothe a king troubled by a bad spirit.
I killed a champion of the Philistines with a sling and a stone.
The prophet Nathan confronted me with a parable about a poor man's lamb.
